description: `Extract` and `Rewrite` operate on exactly one `go.mod` per call. Reject ambiguous inputs (no `go.mod` discoverable, multiple `go.mod` files, or `go.work` workspace) with a typed error explaining which file to point at.

requirements.description: Both Extract and Rewrite must operate on exactly one go.mod per call. The system must discover the go.mod from the provided scenario_path and reject all ambiguous cases with a typed, actionable error. Rejection cases: (1) no go.mod discoverable in or above the scenario_path, (2) multiple go.mod files found within the scenario_path subtree, (3) a go.work workspace file is present. Each rejection must return a distinct typed error identifying the conflicting file paths and instructing the operator which file to point at.
requirements.title: Single go.mod Enforcement and Ambiguous Input Rejection

validation.notes: Test rejection when no go.mod exists in or above scenario_path, error includes path searched
Test rejection when multiple go.mod files exist within scenario_path subtree, error lists all discovered go.mod paths
Test rejection when a go.work file is detected, error identifies the go.work path and instructs single-module usage
Test successful discovery when exactly one go.mod exists at or above scenario_path
Table-driven tests for go.mod discovery across nested directory structures
Extract on a directory with no go.mod returns a typed NoGoModError with the searched path
Extract on a directory containing two go.mod files returns a typed AmbiguousGoModError listing both paths
Extract on a directory with go.work returns a typed GoWorkUnsupportedError identifying the go.work file
Extract on a valid single-module directory succeeds without error
Error messages include specific file paths and actionable instructions so operators can resolve without guessing
Typed errors are distinct proto message types (not generic strings) so consumers can programmatically handle each case

title: Single-Module Project Resolution
